Bug_Details:
A field was set twice in the same chained expression. Proto and AutoValue builders provide a fluent interface for constructing
instances. Unlike argument lists, however, they do not prevent the user from
providing multiple values for the same field. Setting the same field multiple times in the same chained expression is
pointless (as the intermediate value will be overwritten), and can easily mask a
bug, especially if the setter is called with different arguments. return MyProto.newBuilder()
    .setFoo(copy.getFoo())
    .setFoo(copy.getBar())
    .build(); return MyProto.newBuilder()
    .setFoo(copy.getFoo())
    .setFoo(copy.getBar())
    .build();
Bug_Explanation: The bug is embedded in the showBug method where setFoo is called twice on the same builder object in the same chained expression, effectively overwriting the previously set value.
Trigger_Explanation: The JUnit test case triggers the bug by setting the same field twice on the same builder object. The assertion at the end compares the result of the buggy method with the correct expected value, which causes the test case to fail.
